DialMetric.description: Dial counts and rates for one region in one time bucket. One record per region per bucket.

average_dps.description: `dials.total` divided by the bucket duration in seconds, rounded to 4 decimal places. Counts every dial attempt, rejected ones included.

dials.description: Dial attempt counts in the bucket.

accepted.description: Dial attempts that were not rejected by a limit.

rejected.description: Dial attempts rejected by a limit.

total.description: All dial attempts, rejected ones included: accepted plus every rejected count.

dps_limit.description: DPS limit in force during the busiest 5-second window, so it compares directly with `peak_dps`. `null` means unlimited. Enforcement near the limit is approximate; `dials.rejected.dps_limit` is the authoritative signal that the limit was reached.

end_time.description: End of the bucket (exclusive), UTC. Five seconds, one minute or one hour after `start_time`, depending on `granularity`.

peak_dps.description: Dials per second, rounded to 4 decimal places, in the busiest 5-second window of the bucket, summed across all call-processing nodes of the region. Counts every dial attempt, rejected ones included, so `peak_dps` above `dps_limit` is expected when dials were rejected. For `granularity=second` it equals `average_dps`.

region.description: Region where the dials were handled. Current values are `us`, `eu`, `australia`, `middle_east`, `canada` and `india`. New values can be added, so clients must tolerate values not listed here. Buckets of different regions are separate records.

DialMetric.title: Dial Metrics Bucket

get.description:
Returns dials-per-second (DPS) metrics for your account's outbound dials made with the Call Control `Dial` command and TeXML, as time buckets with dial counts, accepted and rejected dials, average and peak DPS, and the DPS limit in force.

The result has one record per region per bucket, ordered by `start_time` and then `region`, newest first unless `sort=start_time`. Regions are never summed: the DPS limit is enforced per region, so a cross-region total cannot be compared with it.

Only buckets that saw dials are returned. Treat a missing bucket as zero dials.

Only complete 5-second windows are counted, and a window is counted about 15 seconds after it closes. The newest `granularity=second` record is therefore your live DPS, about 20 seconds old. Request the last minute or two with `sort=-start_time`; the first record of each `region` is that region's live rate (`page[limit]=1` would hide every region but one). If no recent record exists, the live rate is zero.

Results are cursor paginated. Follow `meta.next`, or pass `meta.cursors.after` as `page[after]`, until `meta.next` is absent. No total count is returned.

This endpoint is in development and can change before general availability.

parameters.description: Bucket size. `second` returns 5-second buckets (the finest resolution) and is kept for the last 48 hours. `minute` and `hour` are kept for the last 30 days.
parameters.name: granularity

parameters.description: Inclusive start of the range, ISO 8601 (for example `2026-09-29T12:00:00.000Z`). Buckets that start at or after this time are returned. A `start_time` older than the retention window of the chosen `granularity` is moved forward to the start of that window, and `meta.start_time` returns the start actually used.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: Exclusive end of the range, ISO 8601. Must be after `start_time`. Buckets that start before this time are returned.
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: Sort order of the buckets by `start_time`. `-start_time` (default) returns the newest first, `start_time` the oldest first. `region` follows the same direction for buckets with the same `start_time`. To read the live rate, use `granularity=second` and `sort=-start_time`, then take the first record of each `region`.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from `meta.cursors.after` of the previous page. Do not parse or construct it. A cursor that matches no records returns an empty page whose `meta.cursors.after` and `meta.cursors.before` both echo the given cursor.
parameters.name: page[after]

parameters.description: Maximum number of buckets per page. Values outside the range are clamped to 1-10,000.
parameters.name: page[limit]

200.description: Successful response with a page of dial metrics buckets.
